correctness.rationale: For all m>=4 over C, eliminating x=-z^3/y gives u=z/y and u^4-u^2=y^(m-3). Two outer branches and one x-axis branch always exist; the inner quadratic splits into two analytic branches when m odd, and one primitive quadratic-ramified branch when m even. Residue differentials omega=dy/[2z(y^2-2z^2)] yield outer orders -3, axis order -2, inner order -(m+3)/2 each (odd m) or -(m+2) (even m). Gorenstein finite-normalization duality yields the claimed conductor valuation tuple. Sum of exponents equals 2delta and Milnor identity mu=2delta-r+1=m+7. Independent parity, conductor-sum and Milnor-delta arithmetic checked for m4..30. m=4 tuple is earlier known, not independently new.
